definition_summary: Unless a source explicitly says otherwise, graphs in this corpus are finite, simple and undirected.
A graph obtained from a subgraph by contracting edges; vertex and edge deletions are permitted.
Largest integer r such that G contains a K_r minor; use 0 for the empty graph.
Minimum number of colors in a proper vertex coloring.
An assignment of colors with different colors at the endpoints of every edge.
A nonempty connected vertex set in a minor model; different branch sets are disjoint.
A family of disjoint connected branch sets with an interconnecting edge for every distinct pair.
Seymour's HC(s) is 'no K_(s+1) minor implies s-colorable'; this corpus indexes by minor order t=s+1.
A vertex set with no edges inside it.
Maximum size of a complete subgraph; it differs from clique-minor order.
2|E(G)|/|V(G)| for nonempty G.
In Norin and Delcourt–Postle, d(G)=|E(G)|/|V(G)|, half the average degree.
Smallest d such that every nonempty subgraph has a vertex of degree at most d.
Largest k for which deleting fewer than k vertices leaves G connected, under the source's complete-graph conventions.
A graph whose every proper minor has strictly smaller chromatic number; do not assume chromatic number is generally minor-monotone.
G is s-chromatic-separable if two disjoint subgraphs each have chromatic number at least chi(G)-s; otherwise inseparable.
A graph made planar by deleting at most one vertex.
Vertices represent edges of an underlying graph; two vertices are adjacent when the corresponding edges share an endpoint.
Replace edges by paths with mutually disjoint internal vertices; stricter than an arbitrary minor model.
Disjoint trees, each properly two-colored, with a same-color inter-tree edge for every pair; parity data are part of the witness.
For a list assigned to each vertex, choose a listed color so adjacent vertices differ. k-choosable means this works for every size-k list assignment.
Minimum total weight on stable sets that covers each vertex with weight at least one.
Length of a shortest cycle; acyclic graphs have infinite girth by convention.
Largest vertex degree; a bound on this parameter is an extra hypothesis.
A probability tending to one as n tends to infinity in a stated random-graph model.
No K_t minor is stronger than no K_t subgraph; never substitute the latter hypothesis in a minor-exclusion theorem.

term: Small graph in the linear reduction
definition_summary: Order at most C t log^4 t for suitable absolute C; t remains unbounded.
Sharp uses t-1 colors for no K_t minor; linear uses Ct for an absolute C.
Unavoidability forces a configuration in every minimal counterexample; reducibility rules it out. Both parts are needed.
For a t-vertex target H, absence of an H minor should imply (t-1)-colorability.
